# Useful resources for Data Collection & Managment {#sec-resources}

## R Programming 

### Essential Resources   {.unnumbered}

1. **_R for Data Science_ book:** Hadley Wickham wrote a book on using the tidyverse and [_the online version is FREE_](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/). This is a phenomenal resource on using R to import, tidy, and visualize data. 

1. [**Posit Cheat Sheets**](https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/): help with commands for using the different `tidyverse` packages, RStudio shortcuts and tricks, help with R commands, and more. You definitely want the ones for Data Import, Work with Strings, Factors, Data Transformation, and Base R.

1. **RStudio Keyboard Shortcuts**: A list of the keyboard shortcuts for Mac, Windows, and Linux can be found [here](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200711853-Keyboard-Shortcuts-in-the-RStudio-IDE). 

1. **Where and How to ask for help:**  

  * Hadley Wickham's advice on [how to write a good reproducible  
  example]((http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Reproducibility.html)) for getting help with R  
  * [how to post good questions on StackOverflow](https://www.r-bloggers.com/2011/01/three-tips-for-posting-good-questions-to-r-help-and-stack-overflow/)  
  * The UF [R-users listserv](http://www.r-gators.com/listserv/) is *very* user friendly and a great place to post requests for help. 


### Tutorials and Books   {.unnumbered}  

1. [R Essential Training: Wrangling and Visualizing Data](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/r-essential-training-wrangling-and-visualizing-data/navigating-the-rstudio-environment?u=41282748)

1. [Software Carpentry: Using RStudio for Project Organization & Management](https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-gapminder/02-project-intro.html)

1. [Swirl](https://swirlstats.com/)

1. [R Bootcamp](https://r-bootcamp.netlify.app/)

1. Kieran Healy's [*Data Visualization: a practical introduction*](https://socviz.co/) is my favorite introductory (yet super-comprehensive) book on data visualization with R. If you scroll down to the bottom of the page you can download the datasets and code used to make the figures in the book, which makes life much easier.

1. [So. Many. Resources.](https://paulvanderlaken.com/2017/08/10/r-resources-cheatsheets-tutorials-books/)

1. [ROpenSci](https://ropensci.org/): tools for accessing, manipulating, and visualizing open data

1. [How to clean messy data in R](https://rfortherestofus.com/2019/12/how-to-clean-messy-data-in-r/) 

1. [The Ultimate Guide to Data Cleaning](https://towardsdatascience.com/the-ultimate-guide-to-data-cleaning-3969843991d4)


### Specific Data Cleaning and Management Problems {.unnumbered}  

1. [**Handling dates and times in R**](https://course.naturecast.org/docs/r-time-series-data/r_tutorial/)

2. **Text Mining:** [`tidytext`](https://juliasilge.github.io/tidytext/) package

3. **Working with Qualtrics** survey data: [`qualtRics`](https://docs.ropensci.org/qualtRics/) package

4. **Optical Character Recognition (OCR):** extract text from images: [`tesseract`](https://docs.ropensci.org/tesseract/) package

5. **Extract text & metadata from pdf files:** [`pdftools`](https://docs.ropensci.org/pdftools/) package

6. **Image processing**: the [`magick`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/magick/vignettes/intro.html) package


### Advanced R Packages for Data Management {.unnumbered}  

1. [`DataCurator`](https://github.com/qcif/data-curator) package: 'a simple desktop data editor to help describe, validate and share usable open data'.

1. [RegExr](https://regexr.com/): online tool to learn, build, & test Regular Expressions (RegEx / RegExp) 

1. [janitor](https://github.com/sfirke/janitor) (cleanup of file names, etc.) 

2. [`knitr`](https://kbroman.org/knitr_knutshell/pages/overview.html) overview: reproducible documents with R

1. [qualtRics](https://docs.ropensci.org/qualtRics/)   


### Slide Presentations   {.unnumbered}  

1. Make [slide presentations with R](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/lesson-11.html)

## Discipline-specific Resources

### History    {.unnumbered}  

1. [`historydata`](https://github.com/ropensci/historydata) package: Sample data sets for historians learning R. They include population, institutional, religious, military, and prosopographical data suitable for mapping, quantitative analysis, and network analysis.

2. [*The Programming Historian*](https://programminghistorian.org/) Website: wide range of topics, from text analysis to OpenRefine
